convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load '3XMA_Ishimoku' custom indicator and includes external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh). The 3XMA_Ishimoku indicator implements triple smoothed high/low channels with Ishimoku-style logic that must be manually reimplemented in Python. However, the trading logic itself is straightforward (crossover signals), making conversion manageable but not automatic.

custom_logic_notes: The 3XMA_Ishimoku indicator computes 3 layers of smoothed high/low channels with periods (3,6,9) using configurable smoothing methods (default SMA) and smoothing depths (8,25,80). The central XMA line crosses above/below the channel envelope (MathMax/MathMin of Up and Dn channel lines) to generate signals. Signal detection uses a 2-bar lookback: previous bar XmaValue was outside envelope AND current bar XmaValue is inside or crossed back, confirming a crossover. The Ishimoku aspect refers to the high/low extremum channel approach similar to Ichimoku cloud construction. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar (not the forming bar), which reduces repainting. The BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose booleans allow independently enabling/disabling each trade direction and exit type. LoadHistory() call ensures sufficient bar data is available before signal detection.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement 3XMA_Ishimoku indicator: (1) compute rolling max(HIGH, Up_period) and min(LOW, Dn_period) for each of the 3 period sets, (2) apply configured smoothing (SMA by default) with depths 8/25/80 to both upper and lower extremum series, (3) combine the 3 smoothed upper lines into UpValue and 3 smoothed lower lines into DnValue, (4) compute XmaValue as the smoothed central line. Then entry logic is: XmaValue[1]>MathMax(UpValue[1],DnValue[1]) AND XmaValue[0]<=MathMax(UpValue[0],DnValue[0]) → buy; XmaValue[1]<MathMin(UpValue[1],DnValue[1]) AND XmaValue[0]>=MathMin(UpValue[0],DnValue[0]) → sell. Position sizing: if MM<0 use |MM| as lot; if MM>0 use as deposit fraction. Fixed SL=1000 points, TP=2000 points. Signal reversal closes opposite positions. Trade only on new bar at H4. The CXMA.GetStartBars() function from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh determines the minimum bars needed for warmup - for SMA this equals the period length. Will need to reverse-engineer the 3XMA_Ishimoku indicator source to replicate exact buffer calculations.
